intervals.label: federal funding approved
intervals.locator: press release of 1 June 1999, paragraph on the history of the project
intervals.note: Start at month precision: the Fermilab dedication release says federal funding was approved in October 1991 (an Illinois challenge grant of 1991 had already paid for environmental and design studies). The end is the groundbreaking of the next interval. Added 2026-10-25: before this the record began with an unsourced 'earliest 1968' bound.
intervals.quote: Federal funding for the project was approved in October 1991, and construction got underway in 1993, after extensive R&D.

intervals.label: construction
intervals.locator: Fermilab History and Archives, page 'Accelerator History', section 'Main Injector'
intervals.note: Groundbreaking on 22 March 1993 (Fermilab History and Archives); the dedication release likewise says construction 'got underway in 1993'. The Main Injector Technical Design Handbook (Chapter 1, PDF p. 5) says "Construction on the FMI project was initiated in June, 1992." and the PAC 1999 paper says the project received first funding in FY92, so project work (design, procurement, R&D) began before the 1993 groundbreaking of the tunnel. Ring civil construction was finished in 1997 and the ring's technical components were installed by 1998; beamline construction towards the Tevatron began in September 1997 and installation continued into late 1998 (PAC 1999 paper, section 1). The end is the start of ring commissioning (next interval). The start carries `earliest` 1992-06 for the handbook's statement (added 2026-10-25 after review).
intervals.quote: The lab broke ground on the Main Injector on March 22, 1993.

intervals.label: ring commissioning (weekend beam studies)
intervals.locator: PAC 1999 paper MOCL3, §2 'Commissioning schedule'; PDF p. 1 (proceedings p. 31)
intervals.note: Ring commissioning began in September 1998 on weekends only, while installation continued during the week. The paper dates the 120 GeV and 150 GeV commissioning goals to 27 and 28 November (year not printed there; the paper was written for PAC 1999 in March 1999). The end is the dedication of 1 June 1999 (next interval).
intervals.quote: The commissioning of the Main Injector (MI) ring began in September 1998.

intervals.label: operating (dedicated 1 June 1999)
intervals.locator: start: Fermilab press release of 1 June 1999 (dateline 'June 1'); end: see the following interval (Fermilab PAC report, April 2026 meeting, findings on accelerator status)
intervals.note: Start is the dedication of 1 June 1999 ("It was dedicated on June 1, 1999.", Fermilab History and Archives; the release says the machine 'officially began its life'; the history page adds that it began delivering protons to the Tevatron in 1999); beams had been accelerated in the ring since the commissioning weekends of 1998 (previous interval). Collider (Run II) operation started in March 2001 and NuMI data taking on 20 May 2005. REPLACED 2026-10-25: the earlier start ('in operation by 2005; earliest 1968') was an evidence date, not a commissioning date, and made the map draw the Main Injector in 1970. END ADDED 2026-10-25: "The MI has not operated since July 2024" (Fermilab PAC, April 2026 meeting); "Following the record achievement [1.018 MW to NuMI, June 2024], the Main Injector complex suffered a series of failures that have prevented NuMI beam." (IPAC'26). Previously open-ended. Review 2026-10-25: the start is the dedication ceremony (the interval is marked 'approximate'), not the first beam delivered to the Tevatron, which the history page dates only to 1999.

intervals.label: no Main Injector beam (transformer failures)
intervals.locator: Fermilab PAC report April 2026; PAC NuMI mini-meeting report July 2025 ("There was no beam delivery for MI since 2024"); PDF p. 2 of the April 2026 PAC report
intervals.note: Start at month precision. Restart is a plan, not a report: the PAC report of the April 2026 meeting (posted June 2026) says "A 20 week run is planned from October 2026 to Feb 2027 to run NuMI. The long shutdown is planned for 2028-29." It adds that the repaired transformers were due by 15 September, two weeks before the 1 October NuMI start. No source dated after July 2026 was found that confirms the restart, so the shutdown is left in place at 2026-10-25 and should be re-checked. The rest of the complex (Linac, Booster, Booster Neutrino Beam) kept running. UPDATE 2026-10-25: the PAC report of the 1-4 September 2026 meeting (posted October 2026) is the newest source: "Beam has already been established in Linac and Booster (Aug 26), MI will start up on September 21, stable beam is planned for October 1"; 6 of the 8 transformers were operational (3 at the April meeting; at least 2 Kautz transformers are needed for full-energy MI operation) and a spare is due in December. That is still a plan written before 21 September: no source dated after that was reachable (Fermilab newsroom has no item on a restart; indico.fnal.gov, fnal.gov operations pages and the NOvA/Mu2e/FTBF sites refused non-browser access), so the shutdown is kept and the planned end stays at month precision (2026-10).
intervals.quote: The MI has not operated since July 2024

intervals.label: NuMI run (planned: 12 weeks, stretch goal 20)
intervals.locator: Public PAC report of the 1-4 September 2026 meeting, PDF p. 4
intervals.note: A schedule, not a reported event. April 2026 PAC report: a 20-week run planned October 2026 to February 2027 (FY27 NuMI run already cut from 30 to 20 weeks for budget; the PAC thought 12 weeks would suffice). Sept 2026 PAC report: "The plan is for 12 weeks of operation in FY27, with a stretch goal of 20 weeks of operation, with a focus on the NuMI beam"; MI start-up planned 2026-09-21, stable beam 2026-10-01. Whether the run started is not confirmed by any fetched source as of 2026-10-25. The planned end (2027-02) is the 20-week stretch case from the April report; a 12-week run from 1 October would end near the end of December 2026.
intervals.quote: The plan is for 12 weeks of operation in FY27, with a stretch goal of 20 weeks of operation, with a focus on the NuMI beam.

name: Fermilab Main Injector
notes: Design energy 150 GeV per the NuMI beam paper; 120 GeV is the neutrino-production operating point.

beam_energy.locator: §2 NuMI Beam Components, first paragraph; arXiv PDF p. 6
beam_energy.note: Operating energy for neutrino production; the design energy is 150 GeV.
beam_energy.quote: The NuMI beam is presently the world's most powerful neutrino beam and is produced by the 120 GeV protons extracted from the Fermilab Main Injector.

circumference.locator: §5 Post-MINOS Plans and Developments; arXiv PDF p. 60
circumference.quote: The Recycler is a fixed energy machine of 8 GeV located on the top of the MI with the same circumference of 3.3 km.

summary.plain: A 3.3-kilometre ring that accelerates protons to 120 billion electronvolts. Its beam makes the NuMI neutrinos today and will make the LBNF beam for DUNE.
summary.technical: 3.3 km circumference proton synchrotron, design energy 150 GeV, operated at 120 GeV for neutrino production; slip-stacked Booster batches are loaded via the Recycler. Source of the NuMI beam and of the future LBNF beam.
